title: MLS NEXT announces fifth annual All-Star Game in North Carolina on July 27
text:
MLS NEXT announces fifth annual All-Star Game in North Carolina on July 27
MLS NEXT announced on June 24 the player selections and details for the fifth annual MLS NEXT All-Star Game presented by Allstate. The match will feature 44 of the top youth soccer players from across the United States and Canada, including Chicago Fire Academy midfielder Christopher Morales, at Mecklenburg County Sportsplex in Matthews, North Carolina. The game is scheduled for Monday, July 27, at 7:30 p.m. Eastern Time and will be streamed live on MLS’ YouTube channel and MLSsoccer.com.
Fans in Charlotte can attend the event with free admission during MLS All-Star week. Registration for tickets is available online. Luis Robles, General Manager of Sporting Operation for MLS NEXT, said, “Selection to the MLS NEXT All-Star Game presented by Allstate is a tremendous accomplishment and a reflection of the trajectory of these players as they continue to develop on and off the field. This event brings together some of the top young talent from across North America and provides a platform to celebrate their achievements while highlighting the connectivity of the MLS player pathway. We congratulate all of the players selected and look forward to watching them represent their clubs and communities in Charlotte.”
The week’s events include team training sessions, participation in programming activities throughout MLS All-Star Week, as well as involvement in other showcase events such as the 2026 MLS All-Star Skills Challenge presented by AT&T on July 28 and the main MLS All-Star Game presented by Chime on July 29.
Players eligible for selection were born between 2009-2011 and must have competed either during this season or participated in one or more premier events organized by MLS NEXT such as Fest, Flex (presented by Allstate), Generation adidas Cup or Cup Playoffs following completion of both regular season play (2025-26) and this year’s Cup tournament.
The East team will be coached by Jordan Melia, head coach for Charlotte FC U18s since his arrival in Queen City in 2024; he guided his squad to a runner-up finish during this past regular season. The West squad will be led jointly by Seattle Sounders FC U15 head coach Ethan O’Neill—who joined Seattle’s academy from Ireland—and Matt Dorman, who became Sounders’ U16 head coach after serving previously as developmental analyst.
Chicago Fire FC competes professionally within Major League Soccer conferences with a roster that includes youth development programs fostering soccer growth throughout Midwest communities; it also utilizes Soldier Field for matches while advancing community initiatives inspired by its crest referencing Chicago’s history, according to its official website.
